text: Thomas Reid held that we have a natural, rational disposition to accept what others sincerely tell us; he called this the principle of ___.
explanation: Reid paired the principle of credulity (the disposition to believe testimony) with the principle of veracity (the disposition to tell the truth); together they make testimony a basic source on which trust is the default and distrust bears the burden of proof. This anti-reductionist stance contrasts sharply with Hume's demand for prior inductive grounds before testimony may be trusted. The expected term is 'credulity'.
